title: University Published Paper Reproducibility Assessment Protocol
author: Scott C Edmunds
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6yahfse

steps.title: Identify Assigned Papers
steps.instruction: Locate the assigned papers using the provided spreadsheet.

steps.title: Access the Paper
steps.instruction: Open the first assigned paper by clicking on its identifier (handle, URL, etc.) and locating it via its DOI.

steps.title: Screen for Data Presence
steps.instruction: Quickly scan the paper and any supplemental files to determine if supporting data exists.

substeps.instruction: If no data is present (e.g., opinion article, erratum, purely theoretical), mark the paper as not having data and proceed to the next paper on the list.

steps.title: Locate Data within the Manuscript
steps.instruction: Spend 5-10 minutes reviewing the manuscript to understand the experiments performed and the data produced.

substeps.instruction: Check the Methods and Results sections.
Check for a specific 'Data Availability' section (e.g., in the structured abstract/front page or 'Supporting information' section at the end).

steps.title: Document Data Accessibility
steps.instruction: Determine and note where the data is located.

substeps.instruction: Note if data is within the manuscript (figures, tables, supplemental files) or accessible via external sources (database accession numbers, URLs, or data DOIs to repositories like figshare, zenodo, or Dryad).
If data is available only on request, note the reasons given and the contact details for access.
Specifically note in the spreadsheet comments if raw data is available.

steps.title: Verify External Data Sources
steps.instruction: Test all mentioned external data sources to ensure they are functional.

substeps.instruction: For database accession numbers: Access the mentioned database (e.g., NCBI) and search for the accession number.
For URLs or DOIs: Click the link to verify it works.
Confirm that the actual datasets are available for download and not just a landing page.

steps.title: Summarize and Report Results
steps.instruction: Input all findings into the spreadsheet and provide an overall rating of data availability.

substeps.instruction: Rate the data as 'available without restriction', 'available on request', or 'missing'.
Repeat the entire process for the next paper on the list.
Once all papers are assessed, send the results to the teacher for marking and collation.
